description.value: A group campsite on the Heritage-designated Cowichan River, celebrated for salmon and steelhead, with a cycling rail trail and restored trestle viewpoints right at hand; note this is a group site billed at a minimum of 15 adults — suited to organized riding clubs, not solo tourers — and it closes in winter with no water off-season.

address.value: Riverbottom Rd W, Lake Cowichan, BC V0R 2G0, Canada

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms this is a group campsite within Cowichan River Provincial Park, managed by BC Parks. The group camping page states regular group camping charges a minimum of 15 adults and youth groups require at least 12 people — this is not suitable for individual touring cyclists. The park is adjacent to the Trans Canada Trail on a former rail corridor, making the broader park highly relevant to cyclists, but this specific group-only campsite is a poor fit for individual WWC directory users. Reservations are confirmed via camping.bcparks.ca. No amenity details (water, showers, shelters) are provided for this specific campsite on the website.
concerns: Group campsite only — minimum 15 adults (regular) or 12 people (youth group); not usable by individual touring cyclists
No address or phone in OSM; BC Parks general contact (1-800-689-9025) is for the entire park system, not this campsite specifically
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a group-only campsite with a 15-person minimum for regular groups. Individual touring cyclists cannot book it. The broader Cowichan River Park regular campground would be a better WWC candidate; this specific group site has limited utility for the typical directory user.
enrichment_extras.notes: Cowichan River Park itself is excellent for cycling — adjacent to Trans Canada Trail on former rail corridor. If a regular frontcountry campsite exists in the same park, that would be a stronger WWC listing.

wow_evidence: group site billed at a minimum of 15 adults — suited to organized riding clubs, not solo tourers
